# Incident Report: Malware Infection — DESKTOP-H8ALZBV

**Evidence source:** `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 frames, ~32 minutes of traffic). No IDS/Suricata alert files were present alongside the pcap — this analysis is derived entirely from raw packet inspection with tshark.

## Infected host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 10.8.15.133 |
| MAC address | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 (Intel NIC vendor) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV |
| AD domain | LAFONTAINEBLEU.ORG (NetBIOS: LAFONTAINEBLEU) |
| Logged-in user | plucero (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString from 10.8.15.133 to DC 10.8.15.4) |

Hostname and MAC were cross-confirmed via DHCP request, NBNS name registration, and ARP.

## Malware family

**Behavioral attribution — not signature-confirmed** (no AV/IDS/YARA alert artifacts were present in the evidence to cross-check against). Based on the observed infection chain and traffic fingerprint, this is consistent with a **DarkGate** infection delivered through a **GootLoader-style oversized JScript dropper**:

- The initial payload is a 6.99 MB `.js` file that is >99% inert padding (scraped technical/report text wrapped in `/* ... */` comment blocks) around a handful of real statements, including a `WScript.Sleep(10000)` evasion delay — a well-known anti-sandbox/anti-AV bulk-padding technique used by JS-based droppers of this type.
- The follow-on payload is fetched using `bitsadmin`/BITS (`User-Agent: Microsoft BITS/7.8`) directly from the same actor's raw IP — a known LOLBin technique to blend malicious downloads into legitimate-looking OS traffic.
- The resulting C2 beacon has a distinctive fingerprint: HTTP GET/POST requests to `/` on a bare IP (no domain), carrying the entire encrypted payload inside a long base64-style `Cookie` header (GET) or as an encrypted binary POST body, with a malformed `User-Agent: Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` — note the spurious spaces around the slash in "Mozilla / 5.0", a known implementation quirk associated with DarkGate's HTTP C2 client. Traffic also carries `Cache-Control: no-cache` and `Connection: Keep-Alive` on every beacon.

Because this identification rests on traffic pattern/TTP recognition rather than a matched detection signature, treat the family name as **investigative, not forensically certain** — submit the extracted payload hashes to your AV/sandbox tooling to confirm.

## Timeline

| Time (UTC+4, as in pcap) | Event |
|---|---|
| 04:10:58 | GET to `quote.checkfedexexp.com` — fake FedEx-tracking lure delivers a ZIP archive disguised as an invoice |
| 04:11:24 | TLS session to `business.checkfedexexp.com` (same phishing infrastructure, `/data-privacy` tracking page) |
| 04:11:59 | Victim host uses Windows BITS to fetch a PE32+ DLL directly from the C2 IP |
| 04:13:00 – 04:42:26 | Continuous encrypted HTTP beaconing to C2 IP `72.5.43.29:80` (306 GET/POST requests to `/`, ~10 second interval, still active at end of capture) |

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — persistent HTTP beacon endpoint (GET/POST `/`, encrypted Cookie/body payloads, malformed "Mozilla / 5.0" MSIE6 UA); also served the second-stage DLL over BITS.

**Malicious domains:**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` — resolves to 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 (Cloudflare-fronted)
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` — resolves to 172.67.170.159, 104.21.55.70 (Cloudflare-fronted)

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — returns the malicious ZIP
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — second-stage DLL fetched via BITS

**Transferred files:**

| File | Delivered via | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| ZIP archive (download from `quote.checkfedexexp.com`) | HTTP GET | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (extracted from ZIP, 6,990,020 bytes) | inside ZIP | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (PE32+ x64 DLL, 159,232 bytes) | BITS GET from `72.5.43.29` | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` |

## Recommended actions
- Isolate DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133) from the network immediately; C2 traffic was still active at the end of the capture.
- Reset credentials for user `plucero` and force Kerberos ticket invalidation (host had recent AD authentication to DC 10.8.15.4).
- Block `72.5.43.29`, `quote.checkfedexexp.com`, and `business.checkfedexexp.com` at the perimeter/DNS layer.
- Submit the three SHA256 hashes above to your AV/EDR and any offline malware sandbox to confirm the DarkGate/GootLoader attribution.
- Hunt for the same "Mozilla / 5.0" malformed UA and root-path GET/POST beacon pattern across the rest of the /24 for lateral spread.
